llm.summary: The skill appears to perform local anonymization as advertised, but its privacy-sensitive workflow depends on mutable, unverified downloads and open-ended Python dependencies.

dimensions.detail: The skill reads selected sensitive text/images and writes anonymized, restored, and mapping files; text outputs and mappings use restrictive 0600 permissions, but users still need to manage those sensitive artifacts carefully.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The install metadata downloads Hugging Face models from mutable resolve/main URLs without checksums, and the uv script dependencies use minimum-version ranges with no lockfile or hashes.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime use is user-directed and mostly scoped to explicit text, file, or non-recursive directory inputs, with documented mapping and output files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: I found no elevated privilege request, durable background service, memory poisoning, or tool hijacking; the text server is loopback-only and auto-managed for command execution.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifacts coherently implement text scan, hide, and restore plus image scan, hide, and category listing for anonymizing sensitive content.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable trusting the current upstream Python packages and model repositories, or pin and verify the dependencies and model checksums yourself. Treat mapping files and restored outputs as sensitive because they can reveal the original private data.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Not accepted as a validated tool-poisoning issue: inspection found implemented scan, hide, restore, mapping, and image masking flows consistent with the stated purpose.
[SQP-2] expected: Model calls include sensitive text and mappings, but the CLI routes them to a local loopback llama-server and refuses non-local server URLs; this is disclosed as on-device processing.
[LP3] expected: The skill needs local files, env-configured model paths, uv, and llama-server for its stated workflow; the main unresolved scope issue is supply-chain pinning, not hidden authority.
[AST4] expected: The subprocess uses I inspected are fixed argument-list calls for lsof, ps, llama-server, or evaluation helpers, not shell-expanded user commands.
[AST3] unexpected: The dynamic import finding is a constant __import__("threading").Lock() use and does not indicate arbitrary module loading.
[SQP-3] expected: The locale examples are multilingual test cases and model-compatibility guidance for type names, not forced user-facing language behavior.
[EA2] unexpected: The cited wording is a caution that public/private name distinctions should not be trusted without verification, not authorization for autonomous high-impact actions.
[EA3] expected: Open-set entity type names are part of the anonymization feature and do not expand the skill into unrelated actions.
[T08] expected: Accepted as a real review concern: mutable model URLs, no model digest verification, open-ended uv dependencies, and no lockfile create a supply-chain trust gap for a tool handling sensitive inputs.
